summary: Sneha pitched Tata Tea's new pack, a Maggi combo and an Aashirvaad festive pack, and pushed for fifty cases of Tata Tea. Hitesh pushed back. He said a Tata Tea price hike has cut sales by about twenty percent, he still has old stock, and shoppers are moving to cheaper local tea. He ordered thirty cases of Maggi and ten of Tata Tea, and declined Mom's Magic as too expensive.
score_reason: An order was taken and schemes were named, but the rep pushed volume without probing the price and old-stock objections, and did not check shelf visibility, collections or the competing local tea.

coaching.tip: You read back the final order clearly (thirty Maggi, ten Tata Tea) and gave a firm delivery date. That builds trust and avoids order errors.

When Hitesh raised the price hike and old stock, ask questions before pitching: how many cases are left, which local tea is winning, and at what price. Then offer help to liquidate the stock instead of asking for fifty cases.
Use the visit to check the shelf (Tata Tea new pack placement, Maggi combo display) and to confirm any pending dues. Also try a small trial quantity of Mom's Magic rather than accepting a flat no.

debrief: Hi Sneha, a decent visit at Patel Supermarket. You came away with thirty cases of Maggi and ten of Tata Tea, and your quick recap of the order was spot on. Next time, when Hitesh ji says Tata Tea sales are down twenty percent and he's sitting on old stock, pause and ask how much stock is left and which local tea is winning before pushing fifty cases. Next step: send the order today and confirm Thursday delivery.
